title: They Like the Energy

source.title: Do Democrats have a 'Democratic Socialist' problem?
source.note: Morning Joe panel after the DSA primary wins in New York (Chevalier over Espaillat); the run 7:42–9:10 is Joe Scarborough (confirmed on the picture, 10-28). Mika Brzezinski co-hosts; the panel is not scored. Cut for The Parallelogram Report ep. 1 as the left-institutional moment (Sailor, 10-28: 'an MSNBC star anchor talking about socialism')

lines.quote: people do not like the Democratic Party any more than they like Donald Trump — I'd be really worried if I were a Democratic leader
lines.note: the warning to his own side

lines.quote: look at New York, D.C., Seattle, Minneapolis, Wisconsin, Colorado — they're having their tea party moment, their Trump moment
a base of very well organized people who are just ticked off — the leadership is weak, doesn't lead them where they want to be led
lines.note: the mechanism: the base vs. the leadership

lines.quote: when that happens you can fill the void with people who often have really wacky ideas
now they're seeing the socialists getting elected — this is the beginning of a movement, not a moment
look at the polls: not just young — young and old Democrats who like socialism more than capitalism
lines.note: the word, with a poll behind it

lines.quote: we can debate whether they could tell you exactly what socialism is, but they like it. They like the energy
lines.note: THE LINE — the word emptied of its meaning, and liked anyway

lines.quote: they like the rage against a Democratic machine; a defining topic going into 2028
if you think they won't elect a socialist, you're not paying attention to what's happening on the ground
